key_insight: LLM-BlockFE turns long text into frozen executable feature programs offline, so risk-control models can gain text-derived predictive power without requiring LLM calls during online inference.
engineering_relevance: The framework is practical for industrial deployment because it shifts expensive LLM reasoning to offline feature engineering while still producing structured inputs for existing downstream models.
method: Incrementally appends immutable code blocks to build feature programs from long text
Uses downstream model performance to score candidate features during search
Adds block-level rollback and interleaved multi-trajectory exploration to avoid greedy local optima
evidence_signal: Across two public and two private datasets, the method improves AUC by 0.0069 to 0.0358 over the strongest baseline, and deployed financial risk-control systems report KS gains of 0.02 to 1.56 percentage points.
watch_item: The approach still requires offline search and careful program validation, so feature stability and maintenance may be challenging as text distributions drift.
paper_title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search
